standard.title: Connaître vs Savoir (Two Verbs for 'to know')
standard.explanation: French has two verbs meaning 'to know' but they are used differently. Connaître (to know a person, place, or thing — familiarity): je connais, tu connais, il/elle/on connaît, nous connaissons, vous connaissez, ils/elles connaissent. Savoir (to know a fact, how to do something): je sais, tu sais, il/elle/on sait, nous savons, vous savez, ils/elles savent. Key rule: use connaître + noun (person/place/thing), use savoir + que/comment/quand/si or + infinitive.

examples.english: I know Marie (I am familiar with her).

examples.french: Je sais que Marie est française.
examples.english: I know that Marie is French (I know the fact).
Do you know Paris (have you been there)?

advanced.title: Connaître vs Savoir — Full Distinction, Nuances & Common Traps
advanced.explanation: Connaître = to be acquainted with (person/place/thing). Full conjugation: je connais, tu connais, il/elle/on connaît, nous connaissons, vous connaissez, ils/elles connaissent. Related phrases: se connaître (to know each other), faire connaissance (to get to know), la connaissance (knowledge/acquaintance). Savoir = to know a fact or how to do something. Full conjugation: je sais, tu sais, il/elle/on sait, nous savons, vous savez, ils/elles savent. Savoir + infinitive = to know how to do something (je sais nager = I know how to swim). Savoir + que/si/comment/quand + clause = to know that/if/how/when. Très utile: je ne sais pas (I don't know — extremely common). Common trap: 'Je sais Paris' is grammatically wrong → must say 'Je connais Paris'. Another trap: savant (scholar) vs connaisseur (connoisseur/expert) — different nuances of expertise.

standard.question: Comment dit-on 'to see each other' en français?
standard.explanation: Se voir is the reflexive form meaning 'to see each other' or 'to meet up'.

standard.question: Je t'_____ à venir au café avec moi.
standard.explanation: Inviter means 'to invite'. Je t'invite = I invite you.

standard.question: Tu _____ mon ami Laurent? (Do you know my friend Laurent?)
standard.explanation: Use connaître to ask if you know a person.

standard.question: What does 'bientôt' mean?
standard.explanation: Bientôt means 'soon'. À bientôt = see you soon!

advanced.question: Quel est le sens correct de 'se voir' dans cette phrase: On se voit samedi?
options: We meet up / shall we see each other
advanced.correctAnswer: We meet up / shall we see each other
advanced.explanation: Se voir means 'to meet up' or 'to see each other' in a social context.

advanced.question: Je vais _____ deux fois par semaine au gymnase.
advanced.explanation: Rencontrer means 'to meet'. Je vais rencontrer quelqu'un = I'm meeting someone.

advanced.question: Complétez: Elle nous _____ à dîner samedi soir.
advanced.explanation: Inviter = to invite. Elle nous invite = She invites us.

advanced.question: On travaille très bien _____. (We work very well together.)
Quelle est la différence entre 'connaître' et 'savoir' ici: Tu _____ mon frère?
advanced.explanation: Use connaître to ask if someone knows another person (familiarity).

standard.scenario: You meet a friend and want to invite them to do something together. Agree on a day and time.
standard.modelAnswer: Salut! Tu veux me voir ce week-end? On peut rencontrer au café. Samedi à trois heures, ça te va?
standard.modelAnswerExplanation: This answer uses key verbs (veux, rencontrer), proposes a specific day and time, and invites the other person to agree.
standard.tip: Use 'On se voit' or 'On peut rencontrer' to suggest meeting. Always propose a specific time so your friend knows when to expect you.

advanced.scenario: You bump into an old friend you haven't seen in months. You want to get to know them again and suggest meeting soon. Use both connaître and savoir, and discuss what you've each been doing.
keyPhrases: Je ne sais pas si tu...
advanced.modelAnswer: Quel plaisir! On ne se connaît pas depuis combien de temps? Moi, je vais au gymnase une fois par semaine maintenant. Et toi, qu'est-ce que tu fais? Tu sais, je viens de découvrir un super café près de chez moi. Tu veux qu'on se voie bientôt?
advanced.modelAnswerExplanation: This response reconnects with the friend using reflexive se connaître, mentions personal activities with time expressions (une fois par...), uses savoir appropriately, and invites future plans using bientôt.
advanced.tip: Advanced speakers should use se connaître for 'to know each other', savoir for facts/abilities, and frequency expressions like 'une fois par semaine'. Use bientôt naturally in conversation about future plans.
